Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-09
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Aisha Malik (Summit AI Head of ML), Tom Rivera (Summit AI Platform Eng), Evan Li (Summit AI CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Goal: scope POC pilot economics and SLAs, define benchmarks, agree on path to procurement/contracting.
- Discussed credits, pilot term length, success criteria (latency, throughput, quality), and commercial handoff.
- Next: Redwood to send draft credits and benchmark plan; customer to provide prompt corpus and security contact.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: ok everyone thanks for joining, we just wanna cover the pilot economics and SLA pathway for the Summit AI POC, I'm Jordan, i'm the account lead
[00:18] Aisha Malik: hey, thanks Jordan. Quick context from our side: we're evaluating two things — latency/cost for live features and hard regression on quality. We have a compliance bar too, so the VPC option's on the table.
[00:35] Priya Shah: great, hi I'm Priya, I'll lead the technical scoping and the benchmarking plan. Can I start with a quick run through of your workloads?
[00:45] Aisha Malik: sure — primary workload is a customer support summarization and a routing classification, roughly 60% summarization, 40% classification. Summaries avg 450 tokens, classifications are short prompts ~30 tokens.
[01:02] Tom Rivera: to add, our traffic profile for the pilot is bursty — evenings in our timezone. Expect peak QPS ~120 during a 20 minute window, steady-state maybe 4-6 qps.
[01:16] Evan Li: and importantly we need to know the cost per 1k tokens to model economics, plus the SLA we can expect for p50/p95 latency.
[01:28] Jordan Kim: excellent, that's the sort of detail we need. For the pilot we usually provide a credit slab and a short term -- typically 30 days with an option to extend to 60 if benchmarks need iteration. We'll propose numbers but want to align on success criteria first.
[01:45] Aisha Malik: success criteria — for us it'd be p95 generation latency under 700ms for short prompts, under 1.8s for summaries, and quality thresholds: rouge-L > 0.55 for summaries on our labeled set, and classification precision above 92%.
[02:05] Priya Shah: ok noted. We'll map those to test harness metrics. About the burst behavior, we recommend including a throughput run with concurrency shaping to simulate a 120 qps 20-minute spike — that helps validate autoscaling and tail latency.
[02:24] Tom Rivera: how do you handle autoscaling for dedicated vs hosted? We are evaluating Redwood Dedicated but concerned about costs.
[02:33] Jordan Kim: good question. For hosted API you get multi-tenant pooling and dynamic capacity which is cost-effective for variable workloads. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput — you'll pay for the reservation but get lower p95s and isolation. For the pilot we can simulate both: run the benchmark against our hosted endpoints and, if you prefer, a dedicated pilot node with reserved capacity. Credits differ by mode.
[02:56] Evan Li: can you give a back-of-envelope for credit consumption? say 50k summary calls at 450 tokens average plus classification at 30 tokens.
[03:08] Priya Shah: rough calc: 50k * 450 tokens = 22.5M tokens; classifications 50k * 30 = 1.5M tokens. total ~24M tokens. If we propose a pilot credit slab of 25-30M tokens that covers a single pass of benchmarks plus some exploratory testing. But it depends on generation temperature and sampling; longer generations use more tokens.
[03:34] Aisha Malik: ok that's helpful. What's the typical pilot credit cap you offer for evaluations?
[03:40] Jordan Kim: we usually offer between 10M-50M credits depending on scope. For a pilot with throughput and quality runs, 25M is a common starting point. We'll include a one-time trial credit for service-hours if you want a dedicated node for a 48-hour run.
[03:56] Tom Rivera: numbering on the dedicated run — if we want a reserved GPU for a 48-hour stress we need to know the hourly burn or equivalent credit conversion.
[04:05] Priya Shah: yes we'll include conversion guidance in the commercial summary. e.g., a single A100-style reserved node equivalent X credits per hour — (note: approximate, we'll confirm based on model/quantization config).
[04:18] Evan Li: and on procurement path — how does the pilot convert to a commercial contract? We have procurement windows next month.
[04:27] Jordan Kim: typical path: pilot (30d) -> pilot evaluation + internal signoff -> contract negotiation for Dedicated or Hosted committed usage. Contracting timeline usually 2-6 weeks depending on SSO, SOC2, and legal review. For enterprise buys we offer pilot-to-production credits that can be rolled into an initial reserved commitment credit if agreed in the contract.
[04:47] Aisha Malik: on security, we will need SOC 2 docs and a KMS/HSM integration. Also audit logs for prompt/response access.
[04:56] Priya Shah: we can share a redwood security pack. For private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and audit logs; for hosted we have encryption-at-rest and key management integrations. We'll note the exact artifacts in the next email.
[05:10] Tom Rivera: will there be an NDA or can we share some internal data now?
[05:15] Jordan Kim: we have an NDA template, but generally we can run non-sensitive benchmark data without an NDA. If you want to send real customer transcripts, we can sign a mutual NDA — we'll follow up.
[05:26] Aisha Malik: good. Let's walk the benchmark specifics. Priya?
[05:30] Priya Shah: benchmark plan outline: 1) throughput/latency run with spike shaping, 2) quality eval against your labeled set (500 prompts), 3) regression tests for hallucination — spot checks with guardrails. We typically run each stage with 3 repetitions to get stable p95 numbers. Expected total run time ~4-6 hours (excluding setup).
[05:57] Evan Li: 4-6 hours seems fine. For quality eval we prefer exact match and semantic similarity metrics — please include both.
[06:06] Priya Shah: will do. We'll also provide a sample harness (github link) and a small docker image to make it reproducible on your side.
[06:18] Tom Rivera: network/egress — if we do a private deploy or VPC peering, what's the setup time? We might need an IP allowlist for the pilot node.
[06:28] Jordan Kim: for porting to a VPC peered/private control plane it's usually 1-2 weeks depending on firewall rules and security approval. For quick pilots we do IP allowlist + short-lived creds. We'll ask for your security team's contact to quicken this.
[06:47] Aisha Malik: we will loop in Naomi from security. Tom will share contact.
[06:52] Jordan Kim: perfect. On commercial guardrails: pilot term, usage cap, and SLA expectations. We'll propose: 30-day pilot, 25M tokens credit, up to two dedicated 48-hour runs if needed, and a basic availability guideline for hosted endpoints (99% during pilot) with no formal financial SLA — formal SLAs start at Dedicated reserved contracts.
[07:16] Evan Li: what about rollback/fallback? If the model degrades in production what's the plan for fallbacks?
[07:22] Priya Shah: we support multi-variant routing — if a high-performance quantized variant underperforms we can fallback to a safer higher-precision variant automatically. For the pilot we can test degradation scenarios. Note: KV cache mis-transcripts aside, we also provide prefix caching to reduce token spend on repeated context.
[07:43] Tom Rivera: curious — how do you measure quality drift during the pilot?
[07:47] Priya Shah: we instrument evaluation alerts tied to your labeled test set. If quality drops beyond threshold we'll notify and can pause rollout. Redwood Optimize also suggests quantization patches and prompt adjustments.
[07:59] Aisha Malik: ok, timeline wise we need pilot results before our procurement window on May 12. Is that feasible?
[08:06] Jordan Kim: feasible if we run the pilot week of April 21 and finalize in one round. Proposed timeline:
- 4/11: Redwood sends commercial draft and credits
- 4/13: Summit shares prompt corpus and labeled criteria
- 4/14 - 4/18: dry run and setup (allowlist, creds)
- 4/21: benchmark execution
- 4/23 - 4/25: analysis and report back
That gets you results by April 25 which fits procurement planning.
[08:39] Evan Li: tight but doable. Procurement note — we'll want a One Pager with pricing assumptions and an exec summary for our finance team.
[08:47] Jordan Kim: we'll include a commercial one-pager and an appendix with credit conversion and dedicated hourly equivalents.
[08:55] Tom Rivera: a couple technical clarifications: 1) model choice, are you recommending an open Llama variant or something finetuned? 2) tokenization differences across models can affect counts.
[09:06] Priya Shah: good points. We'll propose two model variants: a high-throughput quantized variant (fast, cheaper) and a higher-precision variant for quality. We'll show tokenization-adjusted estimates in the commercial summary. For pilot, we can run both and include conversion factors (token counts, p95 deltas).
[09:23] Aisha Malik: on pricing — will the pilot credits convert to committed spend if we proceed?
[09:29] Jordan Kim: we can apply unused pilot credits towards a first reserved capacity commitment if both parties agree during contracting. We'll note that recapture clause in the draft.
[09:40] Evan Li: any limits around model access for compliance? e.g., data residency in EU? We're global, need logs kept in region.
[09:48] Priya Shah: region-specific deployments are available on Redwood Private; hosted has region options — we'll confirm data residency and log retention options.
[09:57] Tom Rivera: let's talk about acceptance criteria again — you mentioned automated regression alerts, but for us acceptance is two-part: technical acceptance (metrics hit) and business acceptance (stakeholder signoff). We have to loop product and legal.
[10:10] Jordan Kim: understoood — we'll include both in the pilot success doc: metric thresholds (p95/p50/quality) + stakeholder approvals (Aisha signoff + product rep). For procurement path we'll include playbooks for commercial handoff.
[10:25] Aisha Malik: small nit — can you include cost sensitivity tests? e.g., if we quantize to int8 how much does p95 change and what's the cost delta.
[10:34] Priya Shah: yes, that's part of Redwood Optimize recommendations. We'll include quantization A/B runs and show per-token price deltas.
[10:43] Jordan Kim: ok, let's capture explicit next steps — Jordan to send credit slab and one-pager, Priya to share benchmark harness and sample prompts, Aisha to send corpus and Naomi from security contact. Also schedule the 2-hour benchmark execution window in week of 4/21.
[11:01] Aisha Malik: i'll get corpus to you by 4/13 and loop Naomi.
[11:05] Evan Li: i'll coordinate procurement calendar. If pilot looks good we'll aim to convert to a reserved 6-12 month commit.
[11:12] Tom Rivera: final question — are there any upfront fees for the pilot?
[11:16] Jordan Kim: no upfront fees for the pilot itself, it's credit-based. For dedicated reserved pilot nodes there may be a refundable deposit if we need to schedule hardware — we'll include options.
[11:29] Priya Shah: I'll send a runbook that includes exact test commands, env vars, and a sample docker image. That will help your infra team reproduce the runs.
[11:40] Jordan Kim: great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the commercial draft and benchmark plan and propose two slots for the benchmark run.
[11:50] Aisha Malik: thanks, talk soon.
[12:00] (call ends)
